rules: Track established facts separately from assumptions and beliefs.
A character can act on a belief, but cannot use information they have not acquired.
Give each decision an immediate goal and an observable response or failure.
Narration should explain a motive, expectation, cost or changed interpretation rather than inventory visible actions.
New information should change a belief, a goal, the available choices or the stakes.
Reserve time for the audience to anticipate or interpret a development.
A cliffhanger must pay off an earlier clue and leave a specific connected question open.
Do not certify dramatic quality from structural checks; require editorial/listening review.
